front: Optimized Bubble Sort: best-case complexity, and what triggers it?
back: Θ(n) — triggered when the input is already sorted, so the first pass makes zero swaps and the early-exit flag stops further passes.

front: Does the naive (unoptimized) Bubble Sort's iteration count change in the best case?
back: No — without an early-exit flag it always runs the full Θ(n²) comparisons regardless of input order.

front: After the first full pass of Bubble Sort, what's guaranteed?
back: The largest element has 'bubbled' to its final correct position at the end of the array.

front: Bubble Sort vs. Insertion Sort: same Θ complexity, but which is usually faster in practice?
back: Insertion Sort — it performs fewer actual operations per element despite matching asymptotic complexity.
